answer:
Final Response: Recipe: 5-Minute Microwave Nutella Cake
URL: https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/230649/5-minute-microwave-nutella-cake/
Prep Time: 10 mins | Rating: 4.6/5 (61 ratings) | Category: Dessert (Chocolate Desserts)

Ingredients:
- ¼ cup self-rising flour
- ¼ cup white sugar
- 1 large egg
- 3 tablespoons vegetable oil
- 3 tablespoons milk
- 2 tablespoons unsweetened cocoa powder, or more to taste
- 2 tablespoons chocolate-hazelnut spread (such as Nutella), or more to taste
- ½ teaspoon vanilla extract
- pinch of salt (Optional)

Step-by-step instructions:
1. Stir self-rising flour, sugar, egg, oil, milk, cocoa powder, chocolate-hazelnut spread, vanilla, and a pinch of salt together in a large mug until batter is smooth.
2. Cook in the microwave on full power until cake has risen in the mug and is set in the center, 1 minute and 30 seconds to 2 minutes and 30 seconds.

Ingredients: 2 teaspoons kosher salt, or more to taste; 2 teaspoons paprika; 2 teaspoons garam masala; 1 ½ teaspoons ground cumin; 1 teaspoon ground coriander; ½ teaspoon cayenne pepper; ½ teaspoon ground turmeric; 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thighs; 1 tablespoon vegetable oil; 2 tablespoons butter, divided; 1  yellow onion, chopped; 4  garlic cloves, minced; 2 tablespoons tomato paste; 1 tablespoon minced fresh ginger root; 1 cup chicken broth; 2 cups cold water; ¾ cup whole roasted cashews; ⅓ cup sliced green onions; ⅓ cup freshly chopped cilantro; 1  lime, juiced. Cook and stir until fragrant, 2 to 3 minutes. Pour in chicken broth and bring to a simmer. Add chicken and any accumulated juices. 6. Combine water and cashews in a blender; blend on high speed until very smooth, then stir into the pan. Reduce the heat to medium and simmer until flavors blend, 15 to 20 minutes. Stir in green onions and cilantro; taste for seasoning. Squeeze in lime juice. Chef John

Total Time: 1 hr 30 mins (Prep Time: 45 mins; Cook Time: 45 mins).

Ingredients:
- 4 tablespoons olive oil
- 1 onion, chopped

- 0.25 cup chopped Italian flat leaf parsley
- 8 slices lemon, for garnish

task: Find a popular recipe for a chocolate chip cookie and list the ingredients and preparation steps.
answer:
Found the popular recipe 'Best Chocolate Chip Cookies' on Allrecipes (4.6 stars, 19,332 ratings, 14,911 reviews) via site search for 'chocolate chip cookies'.

Ingredients:
- 1 cup butter, softened
- 1 cup white sugar
- 1 cup packed brown sugar
- 2 large eggs
- 2 teaspoons vanilla extract
- 1 teaspoon baking soda
- 2 teaspoons hot water
- ½ teaspoon salt
- 3 cups all-purpose flour
- 2 cups semisweet chocolate chips
- 1 cup chopped walnuts

Preparation Steps:
1. Gather your ingredients, making sure your butter is softened, and your eggs are room temperature.
2. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Beat butter, white sugar, and brown sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and creamy, about 4 minutes.
3. Beat in eggs, one at a time, then stir in vanilla.
4. Dissolve baking soda in hot water; add to batter along with salt and mix until combined.
5. Stir in flour just until no dry streaks remain. Fold in chocolate chips and walnuts, if using, until evenly distributed.
6. Drop rounded 1 ½-tablespoon portions of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets, using a medium cookie scoop if desired.
7. Bake in the preheated oven until the edges are lightly browned and the centers are just set, about 10 minutes.
8. Let the cookies cool briefly on the baking sheets, then transfer them to a wire rack to cool completely.
9. Serve or store cooled cookies in an airtight container.

Abstract: Data attribution methods for Language Models (LMs) are typically evaluated using downstream tasks like fact retrieval. However, existing evaluations vary multiple dataset properties simultaneously, making it impossible to isolate exactly why an attribution algorithm fails. To diagnose these failures, we explore the design space of LLM data attribution, with a primary focus on evaluation. We introduce the Controlled Attribution Benchmark (CATT) for fact tracing, in which we fine-tune LLMs on entirely fictitious knowledge, providing unambiguous ground truth for attribution. This synthetic setup allows us to systematically alter one dataset configuration at a time, such as document redundancy and lexical distractors. With this configurable evaluation, we demonstrate that redundancy and distractors consistently degrade attribution performance. Rather than proposing a new estimator, we examine two design choices that are underexplored: the loss used to compute gradients and how per-token attribution scores are aggregated into a document score. We find that the true causal evidence within a training document is highly localized, but standard methods dilute this evidence into noise by averaging attribution scores across the entire document. We find that replacing standard cross-entropy loss gradients with the negative log-odds gradients surfaces the critical tokens from other uninformative ones. We can then aggregate only the top token scores to improve ground truth recall by 35 to 72 percentage points across multiple baselines on our diagnostic benchmark. The negative log-odds correction also generalizes to FTRACE-TREX, improving counterfactual retraining performance for every method we test, by up to 4.9x.

Title: Complete RO-Graded Tambara Structure of H\underline{\mathbb Z} for cyclic groups

Authors: Dongming Zhang

Abstract: We compute the RO-graded Tambara functor of H\underline{\mathbb{Z}} for every finite cyclic group. We introduce a valuation language for homotopy groups: for prime-power cyclic group equivariant, classes are represented by compatible vertex arrays or by edge arrays. In these coordinates we compute products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions, and norms. Then we assemble the results into arbitrary finite cyclic group equivariant case. Besides the computation, we also develop the Tate compression theory, which is used in the computation. The Tate compression diagram cut an equivariant spectra into several layer, which the homotopy group can be describe directly by each layers. Abstract summary: The paper studies resistive drift-wave turbulence using a three-wave truncation of the Hasegawa-Wakatani equations, comparing two triads that differ only by a small tilt of the long-wavelength mode: one zonal (not drivable by the density gradient) and one a weakly driven drift wave. Period maps in the adiabaticity parameter C vs drive show the zonal triad is almost always regular while the non-zonal triad becomes chaotic. None of these routes to chaos exist when the long-wavelength mode is zonal, demonstrating that zonal flows reduce/suppress chaos in this system.

task: In the Hugging Face documentation, find the tutorial on loading adapters with PEFT, tell me how to load in 8bit or 4bit.
answer: To load a PEFT adapter in 8bit or 4bit, you quantize the base model with the bitsandbytes integration via transformers' BitsAndBytesConfig and pass it as quantization_config when loading the model, then attach the adapter with PEFT. 4-bit: from transformers import BitsAndBytesConfig; config = BitsAndBytesConfig(load_in_4bit=True, bnb_4bit_quant_type='nf4', bnb_4bit_use_double_quant=True, bnb_4bit_compute_dtype=torch.bfloat16); model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, quantization_config=config, device_map='auto'); model = prepare_model_for_kbit_training(model); then apply LoraConfig/get_peft_model or load the adapter with PeftModel.from_pretrained(model, adapter_id). 8-bit: set load_in_8bit=True in BitsAndBytesConfig instead and pass it the same way as quantization_config. Source: Hugging Face PEFT docs, Developer guides > Quantization (https://huggingface.co/docs/peft/developer_guides/quantization).
